title: I vibe coded a free multiplayer FPS for the browser, playable on PC and phone
author: Inevitable_Salad_128
selftext:
When Opus 5.5 came out, I wanted to see what it can do in one shot. Then I kept iterating on that first result, and a few weeks later I have Riposte, a small multiplayer FPS in the browser, very inspired by the first Call of Duty games. 

  
[https://www.playriposte.com/](https://www.playriposte.com/)

Almost everything is code written by Claude Code, with three.js and no game engine. Weapons and maps are made in code, with very few external assets. I describe what I want in French, Claude makes the change and shows me screenshots from the game, then I test it myself on a dev version before it goes live.

I’m not a game dev, I just had a lot of fun (sometimes a little guilty) trying my ideas. What surprised me most is that small precise requests work way better than big ones. One time I asked to rework all the maps at once, it launched hundreds of agents for hours and burned my credits for almost nothing. Also the game feel (aim, recoil, sounds) took me much more time than adding features, and keeping the game light enough for phones was a constant fight.

It’s free and will stay free. I’m curious if some of you had the same experience, and what you think of the result.

comments.author: Embarrassed-Ad-4740
comments.body: Amazing! how the heck you manage to get this fluid and with this quality of assets with vibe coding, im tryng to do a full vibe code game to but im stugling to have a smooth gamplayd and something that dosent look diplo low low low graphic game..

replies.author: Inevitable_Salad_128
replies.body: Thanks! It was a lot of iterations, very focused on one thing at a time: weapon by weapon, sometimes accessory by accessory with reference images when I had ideas... I also asked Claude to build small tools to measure the weapons so it could split the work in small parts

replies.author: ex0rius
replies.body: i tried but i'm running it like 20FPS lol. 32GB RAM, Ryzen 3700x,..

replies.author: Inevitable_Salad_128
replies.body: Thanks for the input, I’ll check why, which GPU model? On my side it’s running at 60 FPS on my Steam Deck for instance, and more than 140 FPS on my Ryzen 3900X + RTX 3070

replies.author: ex0rius
replies.body: RX 580 8GB OC. it's older but it still runs most of the games on high settings. While playing the game, the GPU is occupied around 45% (from normal 0-2% idle).

comments.author: Poodletaste
comments.body: How much money have you spent so far to make something like this ? This must've cost a lot of credits right?

replies.author: Inevitable_Salad_128
replies.body:
Not that much actually. I started with the 20€/month subscription and accepted to hit the limits quite fast, and after one week I tried the 90€/month one, only for October to see what it gives, and honestly it’s more than enough for me. I never even thought about paying for extra credits, I prefer doing one change at a time instead of running many things in parallel that I don’t really control.   
  
It’s surely not the most optimized way, and the subscription doesn’t show the real cost of the credits, but for what I wanted it was enough

replies.author: Poodletaste
replies.body: So I'm guessing this entire project took you close to a month or so to make ? I've never actually paid for ai but seeing all this makes me want to try it out myself.

comments.author: ChezPanini
comments.body: Really enjoyed! Just wanted shorter rounds.

comments.author: maddix_cummings
comments.body: Love the DC Fontaines album cover but I have to be a bit harsh here, have you ever played the first Call of Duty games lmao? Nothing in this is reminiscent of them, from the gameplay to the art. Looks very cool though, good job on running it in a browser especially!

replies.author: Inevitable_Salad_128
replies.body: Since CoD 4 yes, but you are actually right, It's wrong saying I'm searching for the feeling of old Call of Duty... Actually I have more the feeling that I was searching for the game feel of Modern Warfare 2019, at least what I remember about it, but thx for the feedback!
